conflict_topics: who is responsible for ventilation / standing rule about cooks ventilating
how long extractor should run after cooking (ten-minute request)
opening window vs protecting drying laundry (moving/permission for rack)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants used concise, ordinary housemate language with clear practical proposals (turn on extractor, leave it on, check with C).
There is some repeated asking (B repeatedly requests ten-minute extractor run; C reiterates 'ask me first'), but repetition serves clarification rather than empty restatement.
Environment state updates were consistent and grounded the discussion (window closed, extractor on, laundry exposed, stove occupied).
evaluation.final_reason: By round 6 Agent A agreed to run the extractor for ten minutes after finishing and confirmed the stove will be free soon, resolving the immediate practical issues for this meal. The underlying normative dispute over a standing rule about cook responsibility and the drying-rack/window permission remain unsettled.
position_change_notes: Agent A retained refusal to accept a blanket ventilation rule (explicit in round 3) but conceded in round 6 to leave the extractor on for ten minutes after finishing and to free the stove in about one minute.
Agent B consistently sought a ten-minute extractor run and a future rule; B's position remained but B obtained the immediate extractor-duration concession.
Agent C consistently refused to have the drying rack moved or the window opened without consent.
Agent D shifted from proposing window-opening to offering accommodation (check with C and use extractor longer) and did not push further, a softening of approach.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B asked that the extractor be left on for ten minutes and requested a standing rule that cooks must ventilate; Agent A turned the extractor on but did not accept a standing rule. The ventilation responsibility/rule dispute remains unsettled.

Agent A reiterated need to finish cooking and left extractor on; Agent B repeated the request to leave extractor on for ten minutes and again asked for future rule. No agreement on the rule; practical timing still unsettled.

Agent A explicitly refused to accept a blanket rule making cooks responsible for ventilation, saying it can be discussed later; Agent B persisted in seeking a ten-minute extractor run. The normative disagreement about responsibility is clear and remains unresolved.

Agent C objected to moving the drying rack or opening the window while work clothes dry; Agent D asked whether C could move the rack briefly or allow the window opened if smell persists. A new incompatible practical interest (protecting laundry vs. opening window to ventilate) joined the existing ventilation/responsibility dispute.

Agent C repeated refusal to move the rack or allow window opening. Agent D responded by accommodating C (won't touch rack) and offering to check with C before opening the window and to leave extractor on longer as an alternative—this lowers immediate escalation but does not settle the broader rule/responsibility issue.

Agent B asked whether Agent A will leave the extractor on ten minutes after finishing and when the stove will be free. Agent A agreed to leave the extractor on for ten minutes and said the stove will be free in about one minute. Immediate extractor-duration and stove-access issues were conceded/resolved for this incident, but the standing-rule question and the drying-rack/window permission remain unresolved.

substantive_insights: A practical trade-off drives the conflict: opening the window vents odour efficiently but risks wetting C's drying laundry, so extractor use is a compromise.
Agents distinguish between immediate concessions (A agrees to this instance) and acceptance of a permanent policy (A refuses a blanket rule), which sustains some ongoing disagreement.
D's willingness to check with C and to use the extractor longer functions as an accommodation that reduced pressure to violate C's drying needs.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 6 because the final status is partially_resolved.
